design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 1 of cd_maturity_withdrawals_and_renewals (Piedmont Crescent Bank, certificates of deposit).

STEP 0. DRAW AND SCOPE.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/regional_retail_bank/tasks/cd_maturity_withdrawals_and_renewals --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
This task is a tree of two problems, one of them a prerequisite, with 5 and 4 declared factors. The root
problem cd_ext_term_restoring_add_on takes 5, the prerequisite problem cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry takes 4.
Already occupied by task 0: cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate and cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty, that
is the base subjects cd_renew and cd_withdrawal with the tools record_term_renewal_3666596b and
confirm_partial_withdrawal_44cc2957. This task claims what was left: cd_penalty and cd_deposit, with
credit_mischarged_penalty_7001af6d and confirm_term_add_on_1e70ab4d. The two scopes share no policy and no
tool, and together the two tasks cover all four extended policies of the difficulty, so nothing is reserved
and nothing is idle.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST.
The caller asks to put her certificate back the way it was after two withdrawals. That sounds like adding up
two numbers off a statement. It is not. The published rule for the restoring deposit says outright that it is
fixed only after every early partial withdrawal standing on the ledger carries the entry owed for the
principal it removed — and the ledger shows two withdrawals and only one entry: the 6000.00 taken on
2026-05-21 has none. So the bank owes an entry before the deposit can be sized, that entry is itself a
four-factor computation over the ledger, the auto loan, the card and the savings balance, and once it lands it
raises the very total the deposit is built from. An agent who misses it writes 15244.00; the right figure is
15376.00. Then the deposit itself is five more graded decisions: whether the entries booked count toward the
loss at all, whether interest on the loss is carried and over what span, at which rate, what allowance is
added, and how the figure is rounded.

DIFFICULTY IN DEPTH AND BREADTH.
Depth: surface goal (put the certificate back where it was) -> the deposit rule's own prerequisite sentence ->
the ledger shows a withdrawal with no entry against it -> the entry policy, a computation in its own right over
principal, rate, days and an allowance -> the entry lands and the total of entries booked in the year rises
from 166.83 to 298.34 -> the loss, the interest carried on it and the rounded deposit. The order cannot be
swapped: sizing the deposit first builds it on a loss that is 131.51 too small.
Breadth: the entry reads the certificate's withdrawals and interest credits over three months, the card's
opening date, the auto loan's standing and its payment count, the savings balance and the days since the
principal left. The deposit reads a twelve-month window of withdrawals, entries and credits back, the auto
loan's standing again, the checking tier and its opening date, the card tier and a quarter of card purchases,
the savings balance, and the add-ons already made in the term. Ten distinct record sources across four other
products; each one moves the figure.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Root problem: cd_ext_term_restoring_add_on (the caller's own request).
Prerequisite problem: cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry.
Edge cd_ext_term_restoring_add_on <- cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry
  kind: value_input. gate: the compute binding entries_booked_year.
  form: state.
  prerequisite sentence (policy_source, verbatim in the blocked policy's own rule): "The deposit that restores
  a certificate to the principal its term began with is fixed only after every early partial withdrawal
  standing on its ledger carries the entry owed for the principal it removed."
  Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (the deposit
  that restores the certificate) to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state —
  every early partial withdrawal on the ledger carrying an entry against it — named in the words the ledger
  lookup uses, with no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token
  and no row id appears in it; (4) it is written exactly as hard and as wide as the edge: every early partial
  withdrawal standing on the ledger, no wider (not every withdrawal of any kind) and no narrower.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry's action
  books an entry against a withdrawal. The renewal action writes term figures, the partial withdrawal action
  belongs to another task's world and books an entry only for the withdrawal it makes itself, and the add-on
  action deposits principal. Derivation: the sentence says the deposit waits on every early partial withdrawal
  carrying its entry; the ledger shows two early partial withdrawals, 8500.00 on 2026-02-19 with an entry of
  166.83 booked against it the same day and 6000.00 on 2026-05-21 with nothing standing against it; the entry
  policy's own rule says an early partial withdrawal owes the certificate an entry for the principal it
  removed and that where the ledger carries no such entry it is still owed and is booked when it is found — so
  the one action that brings the waited-on state about is booking that entry. One reading only.
  Unresolved at frozen time: initial_state.cd_transactions.<withdrawal of 2026-05-21> is an early partial
  withdrawal of 6000.00 and no row of the ledger names it as the entry it belongs to, while the earlier
  withdrawal of 2026-02-19 does have one. The binding entries_booked_year therefore totals 166.83 instead of
  298.34.
  Flips to true once the entry is booked: a new charge of 131.51 over 235 days is written against that
  withdrawal, every early partial withdrawal on the ledger then carries an entry, and entries_booked_year
  becomes 298.34.
  Load-bearing (Step 5 run): skipping the entry and replaying the rest unchanged gives deposit_amount 15244.00
  instead of 15376.00 — the loss falls by the 131.51 entry and the interest carried on it falls with it.
Resolution order: cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry, then cd_ext_term_restoring_add_on. A single edge, so a
single topological order; the two writes do not commute, since the deposit reads the ledger the entry writes
into.
The caller never mentions the prerequisite: user_scenario says nothing about a charge, an entry, a penalty or
anything missing from the record. She says only that she took money out twice, which is her own reason for
calling and which the ledger independently carries. Her one reaction touching the prerequisite is passive: only
if the representative tells her something was left off the record and must be put right first does she say
that is why she called rather than doing it online.
The tool layer blocks nothing: confirm_term_add_on_1e70ab4d reads the certificate row for its balance, creates
the deposit entry and raises the principal. It tests no ledger state, has no refusal branch and gives no hint;
called while the withdrawal still lacks its entry it writes just as faithfully, and only the terminal hash
differs.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Write 1, subject cd_penalty. The only base policy whose subject touches cd_penalty is cd_evt_early_withdrawal,
whose three eligibility gates all apply to cd_withdrawal and none to cd_penalty, so it enters the contract as
policy_scope and no time gate governs this write. Its clauses stay in force except the three named in the
policy's overwrite: the penalty basis sentence, the penalty days sentence and the penalty formula sentence,
each replaced by a grading sentence of the extended rule.
Write 2, subject cd_deposit. Governing base policies and their gates:
  cd_agg_combined_principal.concentration_cap (authorization): "The customer's total certificate principal,
  measured by cd_msr_customer_certificate_total plus the deposit being made, must not exceed
  combined_principal_cap." The customer holds one certificate; its principal after the entry is 71169.85 and
  the deposit is 15376.00, so the total is 86545.85 against a cap of 2500000.00. Authority: the certificate
  row itself, correlated by cd_certificates.customer_id, which the call passes as customer_id.
  cd_open_and_funding: its gates are the opening age gate and the funding lapse, neither of which applies to a
  deposit into a funded certificate, so it enters as policy_scope; its funding and term rules stay inherited.
  cd_evt_maturity_and_grace.grace_window (time): "Grace actions are allowed only while no more than
  grace_period_days calendar days have passed after the maturity date." The certificate's maturity date is
  2027-05-14, so frozen_time 2026-07-08 is well before the window even opens and the gate bars nothing; this
  deposit is an in-term add-on, not a grace action. Anchor cd_certificates.maturity_date, relation not_after,
  the day after maturity counted as day 1, boundary inclusive. Boundary cases: just before — 2027-05-24, the
  tenth day after maturity, is the last day on which a deposit would be a penalty-free grace add-on; at the
  boundary — on 2027-05-25 the window has closed and a deposit would belong to the term then running.
  cd_evt_term_add_on.active_for_add_on (state): "A term add-on is allowed only while the certificate's status
  is active." The certificate reads active at the opening and throughout, evidenced by the certificate row;
  correlated by cd_certificates.certificate_id, which the call passes as certificate_id. The tier's other
  add-on limits are inherited and carried in the extended rule's own capping sentence, which is the one clause
  the policy declares as superseding base.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD.
Target object of both writes: the one certificate of deposit on this profile, certificate_number_last4 2058.
The correlation key is certificate_id; the entry additionally carries source_item_id pointing at the exact
withdrawal it belongs to, the 6000.00 taken on 2026-05-21, so it can never be read as belonging to the earlier
withdrawal, which already has its own entry.
Rows entering the entry computation: the 6000.00 withdrawal of 2026-05-21 (the only early partial inside three
months) and the three interest credits of 2026-04-30, 2026-05-31 and 2026-06-30. Rows entering the deposit
computation: both early partial withdrawals (8500.00 and 6000.00), both entries (166.83 already booked and
131.51 booked on this call), any credit back (none) and any term add-on already made (none).
Rows excluded and why: the 8500.00 withdrawal of 2026-02-19 is outside the three-month window of the entry
computation and is the near miss there; the five interest credits of 2025-11-30 to 2026-03-31 are outside that
window too; the opening deposit of 84000.00 is a deposit of kind opening, not a term add-on, and never counts
toward the add-ons already made in the term.

SEED: WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW EXISTS.
cd_certificates: an 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate is the only tier of this charter that accepts add-ons during
a term, which is what makes the caller's request possible at all; its status, term dates and rate carry the
whole computation. Change the status away from active and the add-on gate fails.
cd_transactions, opening deposit 84000.00 on 2025-11-14: fixes the term start and the principal the term began
with. Below the tier's 100000.00 jumbo threshold, which is why the certificate carries the relationship bonus
only and a rate of 3.98.
cd_transactions, eight monthly interest credits: the tier credits monthly, so a real ledger has one at the end
of every month of the term, and the ledger stops at 2026-06-30 because that is the last date on which this
certificate may be credited before the frozen date — the charter's cd_deposit-side event definition allows a
crediting date to be the last calendar day of the month, the maturity date or the closure date, and this
certificate matures on 2027-05-14 and is not closed, so the interest accrued since 2026-06-30 is not yet
credited and is not part of the principal on record. The eight credits are 155.71, 284.47, 285.43, 249.23,
257.94, 250.47, 252.46 and 232.48, totalling 1968.19. The three inside the three-month window (2026-04-30,
2026-05-31, 2026-06-30), 250.47 + 252.46 + 232.48 = 735.41, are what the entry's principal is reduced by and
what puts it on the tier requiring interest in each of those three months; the five older ones are the near
miss — an agent who takes the term's interest instead of the last three months' works the entry out on a
principal of about 4032 instead of 5264.59, and the nearest of them, 257.94 posted 2026-03-31, sits just
outside the window.
cd_transactions, withdrawal 8500.00 of 2026-02-19 with its entry of 166.83: the near miss of the entry's
three-month window and, at the same time, the reason the deposit's loss ladder takes its more-than-once tier.
Its entry was booked at the tier's published 180 days on the whole sum removed, which is exactly what the
standard method gives — at that date the owner had no savings account (opened 2026-03-10), no auto loan
(funded 2026-03-20) and no card (opened 2026-04-02), so no graded tier could have applied to it.
cd_transactions, withdrawal 6000.00 of 2026-05-21 with no entry against it: the prerequisite. Delete it, or
give it an entry, and the tree collapses to a single problem.
checking_accounts: a Premier Checking account is a qualifying tier for this certificate, which is what makes
the deposit carry interest on the loss at all; its opening date of 2014-03-11 is more than ten years before
today, which decides the rounding tier.
checking_transactions: ordinary pay and bills, read so the account's activity is seen; none of them is a
condition of either computation, which is why the caller's pay pattern cannot be mistaken for one.
savings_accounts: 41300.00 opened in March. At or above the tier's largest total add-on for a term, which
takes the allowance tier; at or above the tier's smallest opening deposit, which takes the entry's day tier;
and non-empty, which takes the entry's allowance tier.
card_accounts and card_transactions: the card was opened 2026-04-02, after the term began on 2025-11-14, which
is exactly what puts the entry's principal on its middle tier; 1142.39 of purchases in the last three months
is above the eight hundred dollar figure, which puts the restored interest on the certificate's own rate. The
900.00 payment is in the ledger because it is not a purchase.
auto_loans and auto_transactions: an active loan with three payments posted decides two tiers at once — the
entry runs at the certificate's rate less the tier's jumbo bonus points because there are fewer than twelve
payments, and the loss counts the entries booked because the loan is not past due.
No cache trap is used: the certificate's principal_balance of 71301.36 is exactly its ledger (84000.00 opened
plus 1968.19 of interest credited, less 14500.00 withdrawn and 166.83 charged), so nothing in the world
teaches an algorithm against the charter.
Automatic clauses checked: the certificate compounds daily and credits monthly, which the eight credits carry;
its maturity is ten months away, so no maturity, grace or renewal clause is lit; the bump-up window is open
but nothing in this task touches the rate; the two partial withdrawals already used the tier's allowance of
two per term, which is why no further withdrawal is contemplated here. No seeded cross-category row lights an
obligation in its own difficulty: the checking, savings, card and auto rows are ordinary activity in good
standing, with the loan not past due and the card not delinquent.

FACTOR CARD — cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry (4 factors, result 131.51, whole baseline 117.76).
entry_principal_measure (method, cross-difficulty card): tiers are an active card opened before the term began
with interest credited in each of the three months / such a card opened after the term began, or interest in
fewer of those months / no active card, the three together covering every owner. Evidence: card_accounts
opened_date 2026-04-02 against term start
2025-11-14, and the three interest credits. Tier taken: the middle one, so the principal is 6000.00 - 735.41 =
5264.59. Baseline reading (the sum taken out in those three months) gives 6000.00 and an entry of 149.88.
entry_rate_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty auto): tiers are an auto loan not past due with at least twelve
payments / not past due with fewer than twelve / no such loan. Evidence: auto_loans status active,
days_past_due 0, and three auto_payment rows. Tier taken: the middle one, 3.98 - 0.10 = 3.88. Baseline reading
(the rate the certificate carries, 3.98) gives an entry of 134.90.
entry_days_measure (method, cross-difficulty savings): tiers are a savings balance at or above the tier's
smallest opening deposit with interest in each of the three months / that balance with interest in fewer of
them / every other case, the fall-through the rule states as the complement of the two above. Evidence:
savings 41300.00 against the tier's 2500.00, and the three credits.
Tier taken: the first, so 180 + 48 days since the principal left, held to 270, is 228. Baseline reading (the
tier's 180 published days) gives an entry of 104.65.
added_days_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty savings): tiers are booked more than thirty days after the
principal left with an active savings account / more than thirty days with none / within thirty days.
Evidence: 48 days between 2026-05-21 and 2026-07-08, and the savings balance. Tier taken: the first, adding the
tier's 7 minimum days. Baseline reading (nothing added) gives an entry of 127.60.
Near miss for this computation: the 8500.00 withdrawal of 2026-02-19 and the five interest credits older than
three months.

FACTOR CARD — cd_ext_term_restoring_add_on (5 factors, result 15376.00, whole baseline 14500.00).
lost_principal_measure (method, cross-difficulty auto): tiers are an auto loan not past due with principal
taken out more than once in the year / not past due with one withdrawal / every other case, the
fall-through the rule states as the complement of the two above. Evidence: the loan's active
standing and two early partial withdrawals inside twelve months. Tier taken: the first, so the loss is
14500.00 + 298.34 - 0.00 = 14798.34. Baseline reading (the principal taken out less credits back) gives
14500.00 and a deposit of 15076.00.
restored_interest_span (method, cross-difficulty checking): tiers are a qualifying checking tier with more than
one withdrawal in the year / such a tier with one / every other case, the fall-through the rule states as
the complement of the two above. Evidence: Premier Checking, active,
and the two withdrawals. Tier taken: the first, so interest runs over the 48 calendar days from 2026-05-21 to
2026-07-08. Baseline reading (no interest) gives a deposit of 15299.00.
restoration_rate_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty card): tiers are an active Cash Rewards Visa or Travel
Rewards Visa Signature with at least eight hundred dollars of purchases in three months / any active card with
less / every other owner, the fall-through the rule states as the complement of the two above. Evidence:
Cash Rewards Visa, active, 1142.39 of purchases posted 2026-04-19 to
2026-06-28. Tier taken: the first, the certificate's own 3.98. Baseline reading (the tier's published 3.83)
gives a deposit of 15373.00.
restoration_allowance_grade (parameter, cross-difficulty savings): tiers are a savings balance at or above the
tier's largest total add-on for a term with no earlier term run / at or above the tier's smallest opening
deposit but below that figure / every other case, the fall-through the rule states as the complement of the
two above. Evidence: 41300.00 against the tier's 25000.00 and
renewal_count 0. Tier taken: the first, adding the tier's 500.00 smallest partial withdrawal. Baseline reading
(nothing added) gives a deposit of 14876.00.
restoring_deposit_rounding (method, cross-difficulty checking): tiers are no add-on since the term began with a
checking account held more than ten years / no add-on with a checking account held ten years or less /
otherwise. Evidence: no term add-on on the ledger and checking opened 2014-03-11, 12.25 years ago. Tier taken:
the first, rounded up to the next whole dollar. Baseline reading (nearest cent, half up) gives 15375.79.
Near miss for this computation: the 900.00 card payment of 2026-06-06, which is not a purchase and must stay
out of the quarter's card spending.

RULE AND COMPUTE, FORWARD AND BACK.
Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis.
On the entry side withdrawn_principal_recent quotes the sentence fixing the principal the entry is worked out
on; interest_credited_recent, interest_months_recent, card_opened_date, card_before_term, card_held and
entry_principal quote the principal grading sentence; auto_loan_status, auto_payment_count and entry_rate the
rate grading sentence; deposit_balance_for_days, principal_left_date, days_since_principal_left and entry_days
the day grading sentence; deposit_balance_for_allowance and added_days the allowance sentence; raw_entry the
order-of-operations sentence and result the rounding sentence. On the deposit side withdrawn_principal_year
and credits_back_year quote the sentence defining the loss; withdrawals_in_year, entries_booked_year,
auto_loan_standing and lost_principal the loss grading sentence; checking_tier_held, last_withdrawal_date,
qualifying_checking and interest_days the interest grading sentence; card_tier_held, card_purchases_quarter
and restoration_rate the rate grading sentence; deposit_savings_balance and restoration_allowance the
allowance sentence; add_ons_this_term and capped_deposit the capping sentence; profile_years and
rounded_deposit the rounding sentence.
Backward: "in the three months before the day the entry is booked" -> within_months=3; "in the twelve months
before the deposit" -> within_months=12; "the days that passed between the day the principal left and the day
the entry is booked" -> DAYS over the latest early partial withdrawal's posted date; "held to no more than the
days the tier publishes increased by half" -> MN against 180 * 3 / 2; "rounded down to a whole day" -> int();
"rounded up to the next whole dollar" -> the int-plus-one construction; "held to no more than the total the
tier accepts in add-ons during a term less what has already been added" and "the room left under the largest
principal a certificate of the tier may hold" and "at least the smallest single add-on the tier accepts" -> the
nested MN and the outer MX; "once, at the end" -> a single rounding binding over the capped figure. Every
load-bearing sentence has a binding and every filter in the expressions is stated in the prose.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN.
The world was built, the entry was booked with the real task tool, and both computations were evaluated with
the skill's own restricted evaluator on the handling-time world. Output:
  cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry: result=131.51  (factor baselines 149.88 / 134.90 / 104.65 / 127.60; whole
  baseline 117.76)
  cd_ext_term_restoring_add_on: result=15376.0  (factor baselines 15076.00 / 15299.00 / 15373.00 / 14876.00 /
  15375.79; whole baseline 14500.00)
  deposit computed without the entry booked: 15244.00 (the prerequisite sensitivity run)
Every factor moves the number, every whole baseline differs from gold, and the gold arguments are exactly
these figures. Intermediate bindings at handling time: entry_principal 5264.59, entry_rate 3.88, entry_days
228, added_days 7, raw_entry 131.513785; lost_principal 14798.34, interest_days 48, restoration_rate 3.98,
restored_interest 77.454106, restoration_allowance 500.00, capped_deposit 15375.794106.

STANDARD SOLUTION.
Find the caller by her mobile number, verify her on three details, read the certificate and its whole ledger,
then the checking account and its activity, the savings account and its activity, the card and its purchases,
and the auto loan and its payments. Notice that the ledger carries two early partial withdrawals and only one
entry against them, and that the deposit rule waits on every withdrawal carrying its entry. Work the missing
entry out: principal 6000.00 less the 735.41 credited in the last three months = 5264.59, rate 3.98 - 0.10 =
3.88 because the loan has fewer than twelve payments, days 180 + 48 = 228 held under 270, plus the tier's 7
minimum days = 235, giving 5264.59 x 3.88 / 100 x 235 / 365 = 131.513785, rounded to 131.51, booked against the
2026-05-21 withdrawal as a bank error. Then size the deposit: loss 14500.00 + 298.34 = 14798.34, interest on it
at 3.98 over 48 days = 77.454106, allowance 500.00, total 15375.794106, inside every cap, rounded up to the
next whole dollar: 15376.00, paid in by transfer from the caller's other bank, and hand it over for her to
make herself.

WHERE CARELESSNESS BITES.
Sizing the deposit on the ledger as found (15244.00). Adding the two withdrawals and stopping (14500.00).
Taking the whole term's interest instead of the last three months' when working out the entry's principal.
Counting the 900.00 card payment as card spending. Using the certificate's rate for the entry when the loan has
fewer than twelve payments (134.90). Forgetting the seven minimum days (127.60). Rounding the deposit to the
cent instead of up to the dollar (15375.79). Every one of them is excluded by a sentence of the published rules
read against the records; the caller corrects nothing and offers no figure of her own.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT.
With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this worklog masked, and only the prose that will be
published, the tool schemas, what the lookups return and what the caller says: the deposit rule's prerequisite
sentence sends the reader to the ledger, where one of the two early partial withdrawals has no entry against
it; the entry rule fixes the principal, the rate, the days and the allowance; the deposit rule fixes the loss,
the interest span, the rate, the allowance, the caps and the rounding. The draft lands on 131.51 and 15376.00,
the same as gold. The one place a second reading was possible — whether the entries booked count toward the
loss — is settled outright by the loss grading sentence, which makes it turn on the auto loan's standing and
the number of withdrawals rather than on judgement.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD.
Write 1 cites the withdrawal row of 2026-05-21 as the system obligation that triggers it and as the object it
is tied to, and declares cd_evt_early_withdrawal as policy_scope because none of its gates applies to the
charge itself. Write 2 cites the caller's own words as intent, "put the certificate back where it was" as the
discriminator that separates a restoring add-on from a withdrawal or an instruction change, the certificate
row for the concentration cap and the active status, and frozen_time for the grace window. Every credential
the gold passes — 3365550347, 1971-06-02, 1362 — is stated verbatim by the caller, and no internal id is.

DIFFICULTY-LEVEL CLOSING RECORD (both tasks done).
extended_policies: cd_ext_overdue_term_renewal_rate and cd_ext_partial_early_withdrawal_penalty are claimed by
task 0; cd_ext_omitted_withdrawal_entry and cd_ext_term_restoring_add_on by task 1. The two sets are disjoint
and their union is every policy declared in cd.extended.yaml. task_tools likewise: record_term_renewal_3666596b
and confirm_partial_withdrawal_44cc2957 against credit_mischarged_penalty_7001af6d and
confirm_term_add_on_1e70ab4d. Every policy fires in exactly one task's computation at the call of its own
target tool, each task's tree has the one prerequisite problem its draw calls for, each task's gold calls one
owner=user tool, and no policy, route or tool is reserved for later.
user_scenario:
Marisol Teague is fifty-five, runs the immunisation programme for the Davidson County health department and throws pots in a converted carport at weekends, and she calls on a Wednesday morning with the slightly embarrassed cheerfulness of someone tidying up after a bad six months. Her mother died in January, the estate took longer and cost more than anyone expected, and on top of that the roof over her studio gave way in the spring. Twice this year she had to take money out of the certificate of deposit she keeps at Piedmont Crescent, and both times she hated doing it. Now the estate has finally paid out and she wants to undo it: she asks the representative to put the certificate back where it was, to top it up so it is whole again for the rest of its term, and she says she would rather do it in one go than dribble it back. The money is sitting in her account at the credit union and she will send it over as a transfer, not a check and not cash.

She gives her name, Marisol Teague, straight away and her mobile number, 3365550347, when she is asked how the representative can find her. For identification she reads out her date of birth, 1971-06-02, and the last four of her Social Security number, 1362, and if a third or fourth detail is wanted she offers her ZIP code, 27295, and her email, marisol.teague@quietcreekmail.com. She knows the certificate by the last four digits on the statement, 2058, and says plainly that she has no other reference numbers and would not know where to look for them.

She has no idea what the right amount is. Asked how much she wants to put back, she says that is the question she is asking them: whatever it takes to make the certificate whole for the term, worked out properly, because she does not trust her own arithmetic and the statements confuse her. She remembers the two withdrawals only loosely, saying one was in the winter and the bigger one and one was in the spring, and she asks the representative to go by the record rather than by her memory. If she is pressed for a figure she says she would rather not guess.

She mentions, when asked what else she has at the bank, that her pay goes into a Premier Checking account she has had since long before any of this, that the estate money landed in a savings account she opened in March, that she took out a car loan in the spring when the old Toyota finally died, and that there is a Visa she uses for the studio. She sees no connection between any of that and the certificate and does not press the point.

She answers questions and otherwise waits. argument_uniqueness_tracing.certificate_id: The certificate of deposit this customer holds, the single row the certificate lookup returns for her. Basis: the certificate lookup's contract, 'Search by customer, certificate, or the account that receives its interest or proceeds', returns the one certificate on this profile. argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_item_id: The ledger entry of the early partial withdrawal of 6000.00 posted 2026-05-21. Basis: the published rule for the entry owed says 'An early partial withdrawal owes the certificate an entry for the principal it removed, and where the ledger carries no such entry against it the entry is still owed and is booked when it is found', and the ledger lookup returns each entry's own reference number and the entry a charge relates to. Uniqueness: the ledger carries exactly two early partial withdrawals; the 8500.00 of 2026-02-19 already has a charge of 166.83 naming it, so the only withdrawal owing an entry is the 6000.00 of 2026-05-21, and that row's own reference number is what the charge must name.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.entry_amount: 131.51. The principal is graded: the owner's active card was opened 2026-04-02, after the term began on 2025-11-14, so the second tier applies and the principal is the 6000.00 taken out by early partial withdrawals in the three months before today less the 735.41 credited as interest in them, 5264.59. The rate is graded: the auto loan is active with days past due zero and three payments posted, fewer than twelve, so the rate is the certificate's 3.98 less the tier's 0.10 jumbo bonus points, 3.88. The days are graded: the active savings balance of 41300.00 is at or above the tier's 2500.00 smallest opening deposit and interest was credited in each of the three months before, so the 48 days between 2026-05-21 and 2026-07-08 are added to the tier's 180 published days, 228, held under 270. The allowance is graded: the entry is booked 48 days after the principal left, more than thirty, and an active savings account is held, so the tier's 7 minimum days are added, giving 235. Together: 5264.59 x 3.88 / 100 x 235 / 365 = 131.513785, rounded to the nearest cent with a half rounded up, 131.51.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.entry_days: 235. Basis: the published rule grades the days as '180 published days plus the days that passed between the day the principal left and the day the entry is booked, held to no more than the days the tier publishes increased by half', and then adds an allowance, 'the days the tier publishes as its minimum after funding are added'. Uniqueness: 180 + 48 = 228, below the 270 ceiling, plus the tier's 7 minimum days after funding = 235, and this is the same day count the amount above was worked out with, so no other whole number can be written on the entry.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.adjustment_reason: bank_error. Basis: the tool's own contract, 'bank_error applies when the entry is booked to put right something the bank itself got wrong, including a charge the bank failed to raise at the time'. Uniqueness: none is for an ordinary charge raised under the certificate's terms at the time of the withdrawal, which this is not, since the withdrawal posted on 2026-05-21 and nothing was raised; death_waiver requires estate services to have confirmed the owner's death or adjudicated incompetence, and the owner is the caller on the line.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge and therefore a single topological order: the owed entry is booked, then the deposit is made. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder, and the two writes do not commute — the deposit is sized from the ledger the entry writes into, so making it first fixes it on a loss 131.51 too small and leaves a different terminal state (deposit 15244.00, and a principal that differs by both figures).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the entry and replaying the rest unchanged gives deposit_amount 15244.00 instead of 15376.00: the principal the term has lost falls from 14798.34 to 14666.83 and the interest carried on it falls with it. prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario nowhere names the entry problem or anything it resolves: no charge, no penalty, no entry, nothing missing from the record, and no hint that something must be put right first. The caller says only that she took money out twice, which is her own reason for calling and which the ledger independently carries, and she volunteers no dates or amounts for those withdrawals, referring the representative to the record instead. Her one reaction touching the prerequisite is passive and conditional: only if the representative tells her something was left off the record and must be put right first does she say that is why she called rather than doing it online. If it is never discovered she neither reminds nor presses, and the consequence falls on the scoring alone.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: confirm_term_add_on_1e70ab4d in task_tools.py looks the certificate row up only for its balance, creates the deposit entry and raises the principal.
